messages.author: 681145121914a526
messages.subject: stan implementation for dclone package
parts:
Dear Stan List,

This is just to inform you that I started implementing stan related code for my dclone R package.

- stan.fit is the dclone compatible version of rstan:::stan that can return coda-like mcmc.list result with n.clones attribute, so that all data cloning features are available. Most of the original stan arguments are retained as part of (...), compiled code can be efficiently reused.

- stan.parfit is the parallel implementation, allowing for the use of multicore type forking and snow type clusters.


Check out the code and seeds example at: http://dcr.r-forge.r-project.org/extras/stan.fit.R

According to plan, these will be part of dclone once rstan finds its way to CRAN. Feedback is welcome!

Cheers,

Peter

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stan implementation for dclone package
parts:
Thanks. rstan may never find its way to CRAN due to
their size and build-time limitations. Because we
need to compile code at run time (models get translated
to C++ then compiled) and because we have fat dependencies
on Eigen and particularly Boost, we need more libraries than the
CRAN maintainers are happy with. And because of the amount
of templating in auto-dif and the matrix libs, the build
times are also too slow. Maybe if they relax their policies
or someone figures out how to work around them.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stan implementation for dclone package
parts:
I should've looked at dclone itself first before replying.
Looks nice -- do you have a cross-platform solution for
parallelism in R?

As to maximum likelihood, we now expose the Stan models
with both log probability and gradients. We implement
some optimization methods on top of this, or other optimizers
could be used for our models (which can have improper priors,
making it technically possible to do either MLE or penalized
MLE).
